references.text: The ransom system in Israel where each person gave a ransom for their soul to the Lord, as seen here in Numbers where gold jewelry is brought as atonement for the soldiers' lives.
The Israelites brought voluntary gifts of gold jewelry to the tabernacle, including bracelets, rings, and earrings, similar to the gold items mentioned in this text.
Women gave their bronze mirrors as an offering to the sanctuary, an example of giving valuable personal possessions to the Lord's service.
Moses and Eleazar received the gold from the army commanders and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the people of Israel before the Lord.
Blood is used for atonement for the soul; here, gold items are brought as an offering for the soldiers' lives after the war.
Gold and silver from Jericho were dedicated to the Lord's treasury, similar to how war spoils were given as offerings in this text.
Gideon collected gold rings from the war spoils after the victory over the Midianites, corresponding to the gold items gathered here.
King David dedicated silver and gold from conquered peoples to the Lord, a practice that reflects the offering in this text.
